They may come around for another pass.''"
"''Captain Needa, the ship no longer appears on our scopes.|Needa gives orders to Nemet concerning the ''Millennium Falcon''|audio=Needa-TrackThem.flac|}} [[Commander]] '''Nemet''' was a [[human]] [[Imperial officer|officer]] in the [[Imperial Navy|naval forces]] of the [[Galactic Empire]]. In [[3 ABY]], he [[Assignment|served]] as [[tracking officer]] aboard the [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Avenger]]'', a part of the [[Dark Lord of the Sith|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader's]] personal [[fleet]], [[Death Squadron]]. The fleet searched for the [[Echo Base|secret base]] of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]], culminating in the [[Battle of Hoth]], after which the ''Avenger'' took part in the pursuit of the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]'', a rebel [[YT-1300 light freighter|vessel]] that escaped from the [[planet]] [[Hoth]]. During the chase, the ''Falcon'' hid in the [[Hoth asteroid field]] and then escaped Imperial [[sensor]]s by landing on the [[Conning tower|command tower]] of the ''Avenger''. After the [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer|Star Destroyer's]] [[captain]], [[Lorth Needa]], ordered the ''Falcon'' be tracked, Nemet informed him that the [[Starship|vessel]] had vanished. Needa was then [[Death|executed]] for losing the ''Falcon'', which ultimately escaped from the Imperials. ==Biography== {{Quote|They can't have disappeared. No ship that small has a cloaking device.''"
"''Well, there's no trace of them, sir.|Needa and Nemet discuss the ''Millennium Falcon''|audio=Needa-Nemet.flac|}} [[File:Avenger-ESBHD.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Commander Nemet served on the bridge of the ''Avenger''.]] The [[human]] Nemet{{WebCite|url=https://www.starwarsauthentics.com/iSynApp/productDisplay.action?productId=1325533|text=Commander Nemet|work=[https://www.starwarsauthentics.com ''Star Wars Authentics'']|archivedate=20200506234920}} served as a member of the [[Imperial Navy's officer corps|officer corps]] of the [[Imperial Navy]] of the [[Galactic Empire]]. In [[3 ABY]],''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas: Updated Edition]]'' dates the events of {{Film|V}} to [[3 ABY]]. he held the role of [[commander]] and [[Assignment|served]] as a [[tracking officer]] aboard the [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Avenger]]'',{{ShipsandVehiclesCite|4|History of the Ship}} under the [[Commanding officer|command]] of [[Captain]] [[Lorth Needa]]. The ''Avenger'' was a part of [[Death Squadron]],''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]'' a [[fleet]] of [[Star Destroyer]]s led by the [[Dark Lord of the Sith|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] in a search of the [[Echo Base|secret headquarters]] of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. When the headquarters was discovered on the [[planet]] [[Hoth]], the ''Avenger'' was among the [[Starship|vessels]] that took part in the Imperial [[Battle of Hoth|attack]] on the base.{{Databank|captain-needa|Captain Needa}} The [[YT-1300 light freighter]] known as the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]'' was among the rebel craft to escape Hoth, and Vader ordered that the ''Avenger'' and other vessels pursue it, as it carried close allies of his son, [[Luke Skywalker]]. The [[freighter]] managed to hide for a [[time]] from the pursuing vessels within the [[Hoth asteroid field]], but upon exiting the [[Asteroid field|field]], it encountered the ''Avenger'', which had been patrolling the edge of the field. Failing to jump to [[hyperspace]] due to issues with the ''Falcon''{{'s}} [[hyperdrive]], the freighter's captain, [[Han Solo]], flew his ship directly at the ''Avenger'' while Nemet moved over to one of the [[Data pit|crew pit]] consoles on the [[Bridge (starship)|bridge]] of the ''Avenger''. He was leaning over the shoulder of the bridge crew member at the console when the ''Falcon'' flew in close past the [[viewport]] of the bridge, causing the commander to quickly glance up out of the pit. [[File:MKaeAndFriends-ESBBR.png|thumb|right|250px|Nemet informed Captain Needa that the ''Avenger'' had lost the ''Millennium Falcon''.]] Solo then landed the ''Falcon'' on the ''Avenger''{{'s}} [[Conning tower|command tower]], causing the freighter to disappear from the [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer|Star Destroyer's]] scanners. Needa immediately ordered that the freighter be tracked, but after checking his screen, Nemet reported the loss of the vehicle. He confirmed it after checking his screen again when Needa questioned if a vessel like the ''Falcon'' was large enough to have a [[cloaking device]]. [[Communications officer/Legends|Communications officer]] [[M'Kae]]{{Topps|set=2019 Topps Star Wars Black & White: The Empire Strikes Back|cardname=Mark Capri as Officer M'Kae|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/196703/cid/12614769/2019-Topps-Star-Wars-Black-&-White:-The-Empire-Strikes-Back---Autographs-NNO-Mark-Capri}} then informed Needa that Vader wanted an update on the pursuit of the ''Falcon'', and the captain left to apologize to Vader, who [[Death|executed]] him for his failure. The ''Falcon'' ultimately managed to escape without alerting the Imperials, but was pursued by the [[bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett]]. ==Personality and traits== Nemet had fair skin, [[Color|brown]] [[eye]]s, and brown [[hair]]. ==Equipment== Nemet wore a standard olive-gray Imperial Navy [[Imperial officer|officer's]] [[Clothing|uniform]], including a [[belt]] and a [[Imperial kepi|cap]] with an [[officer's disk]]. On his right [[breast]], the commander bore a single [[code cylinder]] and a [[rank insignia plaque]] with two red squares above two blue. ==Behind the scenes== ===''The Empire Strikes Back''=== [[File:NemetsClone.png|thumb|left|300px|Footage of Nemet was reused for the bridge of the ''Executor''.]] Nemet was portrayed by [[Mark Jones]] in the [[1980]] [[original trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']], although the character was only credited in the film as one of several "Other [[officer]]s." Nemet's lines were dubbed over by actor [[James Gleason]] at [[Wikipedia:Samuel Goldwyn Studio|Samuel Goldwyn Studios]] on [[November 2]], [[1979]], with the dialogue replacement cue sheet refering to Nemet as the "Floor Commander."{{WebCite|url=https://www.collectors.com/autograph/star-wars-james-gleason-signed-commander-nemet-cue-sheet-8x/-8280759668287779545|text=Star Wars- James Gleason signed Commander Nemet cue sheet 8x10|work=[https://www.collectors.com/ Collectors]|archivedate=20210929063842}} In the film's script, the character is referred to only as "Tracking Officer."{{InsiderCite|58|Behind the Magic}} Jones appears again toward the end of the film aboard the bridge of Vader's [[flagship]], the ''[[Executor]]'', as footage from the ''Avenger'' was reused; however, this article assumes that this is a separate character. The scenes on the bridge of the ''Avenger'' were shot on Stage 5 at [[Elstree Studios]] at some point between [[April 24]] and [[May 2]], [[1979]].''[[Creating the Worlds of Star Wars: 365 Days]]'' ===Tie-in material=== {{Quote|We can't find them, sir! They've just…disappeared!|Nemet's altered dialogue in ''So You Want to be a Jedi?''|audio=Nemet-altered.flac|''[[The Empire Strikes Back: So You Want to Be a Jedi?]]''}} In the [[2015]] novel adaptation of the film, ''[[The Empire Strikes Back: So You Want to Be a Jedi?]]'' by [[Adam Gidwitz]], Nemet's dialogue is altered to sound more panicked than in the film. The [[2016]] [[Star Wars: The Original Trilogy – A Graphic Novel|graphic novel adaptation]] of the film by [[Alessandro Ferrari]] also alters Nemet's dialogue, merging his two lines together by removing Needa's dialogue between them.''[[Star Wars: The Original Trilogy – A Graphic Novel]]'' [[Suba (lieutenant)|Suba]], a character with an identical rank plaque{{ForceCollection|Lieutenant Suba|star=1}} to Nemet, has been identified as a [[lieutenant]] in [[canon]] media. In the new ''[[Star Wars]]'' canon, Nemet was first identified in the title for a [[2018]] ''Star Wars Authentics'' image produced by [[Topps|The Topps Company, Inc.]], which incorrectly states that the character appeared in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]. The name "Nemet" originated in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, where it was first used on a card in the [[1997]] ''[[Dagobah Limited]]'' set of the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]].{{CCG|set=Dagobah Limited|cardname=Commander Nemet}} In Legends, Nemet also appeared prior to the release of ''The Empire Strikes Back'' in the film's [[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|novelization]] by [[Donald F. Glut]][[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back'' novelization]] and ''[[The Empire Strikes Back Storybook]]'' by [[Shep Steneman]], which were released earlier in 1980.''[[The Empire Strikes Back Storybook]]'' ==Appearances== {{Mediacat|soundcat=Audio files of Nemet|imagecat=Images of Nemet}} *''[[Star Wars: The Original Trilogy – A Graphic Novel]]'' {{Voice}} *{{Film|V}} {{1st}} *''[[The Empire Strikes Back: So You Want to Be a Jedi?]]'' {{Ab|The Empire Strikes Back: So You Want to Be a Jedi?
